sections.html:
Property tax in Dawson County runs through two departments in the same courthouse. The Tax Assessor sets values and receives exemption forms. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and disburses all taxes under Georgia law, and also serves as the state's motor vehicle tag and title agent.

The commissioner is at 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, in the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville. The office answers at (706) 344-3520 on weekdays between eight and five. It has its own site at dawsoncountytax.com and takes property tax payments by phone at (706) 701-2576. The assessor is down the hall at Suite 1201, on (706) 344-3590, and runs a separate website with a property search, a sales search and a tax estimator.

Call the commissioner for the due date that applies to your parcel, and ask the assessor about anything to do with value or exemptions.

sections.h2: Dawson County home values and growth
sections.html:
Dawson County is growing fast. The population was 26,798 in 2020 and is estimated at 35,365 for July 2025, a gain of 32.0 percent. Dawsonville is the only city and holds the courthouse. Part of Lake Lanier reaches the southeast corner, and ridges and mountain slopes run along the north and west.

  • Typical value of an owned home (2020 to 2024): $406,700.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,626.
  • Housing units: 14,876, with 11,573 households.
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 78.7 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,069.

At these values, the 40 percent assessment on a Dawson County house makes for a sizable tax base. Lake and mountain views, forest edges and steep lots all change how a house is valued, so read your assessment notice with those features in mind. The estimator on the assessor's website lets you answer a buyer's question about yearly tax with the county's own tool.

The assessor offers several programs that lower the value being taxed. Most need a 10-year covenant and an application filed between January 1 and April 1.

Dawson County special assessment programs
ProgramHow the land is taxed
Preferential agriculturalBona fide farm property assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40 percent, with a 10-year commitment
Conservation useAssessed at current use value, 10-year commitment, with savings that can top 50 percent in some cases
Environmentally sensitiveCurrent use value for land kept natural and meeting Department of Natural Resources rules, 10 years
Residential transitionalCurrent use value for homes in areas shifting to other uses, 10-year covenant
TimberStanding timber untaxed until sold or harvested, then taxed at 100 percent of value
Equipment and fixturesAssessed at 40 percent of fair market value

If you are selling acreage under one of these covenants, ask the assessor what happens to the covenant when ownership changes. The commitment runs for ten years, and a buyer should hear about it before the contract is signed.

April 1 is the date to remember. Real property returns, personal property returns, conservation use and forest land applications, requests for parcel splits or combinations, and exemptions are all taken from January 1 through April 1. No extension is given for any type of exemption.

  • Regular homestead applications can be accepted year-round, but they must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year.
  • Senior and other specialized exemptions follow the same April 1 deadline.
  • Exemption applications are taken in person only.
  • Once you have an exemption, you do not reapply unless you move to another address.

The county also posts a list of assessment notices that came back undeliverable, as Georgia's O.C.G.A. 48-5-306(c) directs. If you changed addresses or inherited a parcel, check that list on the assessor's website so a missed notice does not cost you the appeal window.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Dawson County valuation
sections.html:
An appeal must be in writing and arrive within 45 days of the assessment notice. Late ones are invalid. The grounds are limited to taxability, uniformity with similar properties and value.

The assessors review the appeal first. If they leave the value alone, a three-person Board of Equalization named by the Grand Jury hears it. A taxpayer or the assessor who disagrees with that result may then go to Superior Court.

Appeal volume has been heavy. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, a county where appeals reach 3 percent of parcels, or 3 percent of the digest's value, gets an extra 180 days to decide them, and Dawson County hit that threshold in 2024. Field appraisers who handle appeals and reviews carry photo identification and drive marked county vehicles. If you have a question about a visit or a notice, call (706) 344-3590.

The levy applies to 40 percent of fair market value, fixed at the start of each year. Millage is set annually, and a mill is a dollar of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value. The money pays for police and fire services, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

Fair market value means the amount a knowledgeable buyer would pay and a willing seller would accept in an arm's-length sale. The assessors use cost, market and income approaches. The market approach compares sales of similar properties, which is why a run of high-priced sales on your road tends to push your value up.

Ask the tax commissioner for the millage that applies to your address, and use the assessor's estimator to test a figure before you compare it with the bill.

Request the balance from the tax commissioner before the sale contract is final. Tax is charged to the owner on January 1, so a seller who closes later in the year may hold that year's bill. Write the split into the contract.

  • Mobile home bills carry their own date. They are due April 1.
  • You can pay at the counter in Suite 1222 or on the pay-by-phone line, (706) 701-2576.
  • If the house is under a conservation or agricultural covenant, tell the buyer and the assessor.
  • If an estate is selling, ask the assessor which documents are needed to update the owner and the homestead record.

Get the payoff in writing and route it through the settlement agent so the check goes straight to the commissioner and you keep the receipt. A cash buyer can close faster, but the tax bill and any covenant still have to be sorted out before the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: What to bring when you visit the offices
sections.html:
A short trip saves a second one. Bring the parcel number or the property address, a photo ID, and your latest assessment notice or tax bill. For a homestead filing, remember that applications are taken in person only, so plan to go yourself rather than mail the form.

Visit the commissioner in Suite 1222 for balances, payments and mobile home bills. Visit the assessor in Suite 1201 for values, covenants, exemptions and the list of undeliverable notices. If you are not sure which office owns your question, start with the assessor for anything about value and the commissioner for anything about money owed.

Buyers sometimes ask for a tax estimate during showings. Pull the number from the assessor's estimator ahead of time and keep it with the listing paperwork.

faqs.q: Where is the Dawson County tax commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, inside the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville. Staff answer weekdays from eight to five at (706) 344-3520.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Dawson County property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's website lists (706) 701-2576 for paying property tax by phone. You can also call the main office at (706) 344-3520 or pay at the counter.

faqs.q: What is the filing deadline for a Dawson County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1. Regular homestead applications can be taken year-round, but one that arrives after April 1 does not count for that tax year, and applications must be made in person.

faqs.q: What is the Dawson County appeal period?
faqs.a: You have 45 days after the assessment notice arrives, and the appeal must be in writing. Late filings are invalid.

faqs.q: What happens to a farm or conservation covenant when I sell?
faqs.a: The commitment runs for 10 years, so ask the assessor how a change of ownership affects it before you list. Tell the buyer about the covenant up front.
